# Curse of Strahd - An unofficial fan game

> A free, single-player, turn-based tactical RPG that plays the whole Curse of Strahd campaign on the 2024 Dungeons &
> Dragons rules. It is an unofficial, non-commercial fan game: not made, approved, endorsed or sponsored by Wizards of
> the Coast, and not affiliated with them. Curse of Strahd, Dungeons & Dragons, D&D and Ravenloft are trademarks of
> Wizards of the Coast LLC.

## What it is

- The whole campaign, from the misty road into Barovia to Castle Ravenloft: 86 places in 19 regions, played in the
  order you choose after the opening chapters, with a Tarokka reading that reshuffles each playthrough and five
  endings.
- A party of four drawn from six voiced companions (Sir Godrick, Liriel, Thistle, Ratatouille, Wren and Kip), or a hero
  you make yourself. You control every party member; the AI runs only enemies.
- The 2024 rules done closely: 12 classes and 69 subclasses to level 11, 443 spells, 147 feats, 125 monsters and over
  540 magic items. Every number on screen can show how it was worked out.
- Turn-based fights on a 5-foot grid that start where you stand, with hit odds shown before every attack, area
  templates that warn about friendly fire, height and flight, breakable and burnable objects, and enemy AI.
- Voiced conversations with skill checks that show who rolls and their chance, a big animated d20, and a Narrator.
- Storybook-style 2D characters in a lit 3D world (an HD-2D look), with weather, day and night, and a gothic interface.
- Four difficulties (Story, Balanced, Tactician, Honour), Skirmish and a Character Lab, achievements, and rebindable
  keys, text size and interface scale.

## Platforms and price

Free. macOS on Apple silicon, and Windows 10/11 64-bit. Single player. Keyboard and mouse; a controller works in fights.

## Wiki (spoilers)

The game's full guide at https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/: every quest's walkthrough, every place with its map, every
person, creature, item (with its cheat code), spell and rule. It covers the whole story, endings included. Every wiki
page also has a plain Markdown copy at the same address ending in .md, and https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/sitemap.xml
lists them all.

- [Wiki front page](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/index.md)
- [Main Story](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/quests/main-story.md): the story's quests in order
- [Side Quests](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/quests/side-quests.md): every side quest, by region and level
- [All Locations](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/locations/all-locations.md): every place, with maps
- [People](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/people/all-people.md) and [Bestiary](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/bestiary/all-creatures.md)
- [Magic Items](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/items/magic-items.md), [Equipment](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/items/equipment.md) and [Where to Find Items](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/items/where-to-find-items.md)
- [Cheat Codes](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/items/cheat-codes.md): every item's code, and how to use one
- [House Rules](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/rules/house-rules.md): where the game differs from the 2024 rules
- [Endings](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/story/endings.md) and [The Tarokka Reading](https://curseofstrahd.app/wiki/story/tarokka-reading.md)
